opener: Father, there's a weight I've been carrying that I haven't put into words for anyone — not because I'm ashamed of it, but because I don't know how to say it without sounding like I'm not coping.
paragraphs: I smile in the group chat and go quiet the second I'm alone with it again. I've gotten so good at the update that sounds fine — "I'm managing," "it's getting better" — that I've started to wonder if anyone would even recognize the real weight if I finally set it down in front of them. You already know what I haven't said out loud. You were there for the part of the story I edited out before I told it to anyone else, and You didn't flinch at any of it.

So I'm not going to perform strength for You tonight. Here it is, unedited: I'm tired, I'm not sure how this resolves, and I need You to carry what I've been pretending is light. Let me stop managing this alone and let You actually hold it — not as a burden I confess once and keep carrying anyway, but as a weight I finally hand over for good. Be the One I don't have to explain myself to, the One who already knew and stayed anyway. In Jesus' name, amen.
bold: You already know what I haven't said out loud
kicker: A Prayer For The Thing You Haven't Told Anyone
footerNote: Save this for the version of you that's still holding it alone
